summary: A satirical piece mocking local education and human capital policies after September 1, 2023, under Education Tsar Mr. John Doe and chancellor Ms. Mary Smith. It lampoons funding cuts, failing technology rollouts, outdated career training, jargon requirements, austerity measures and threats to the arts. It closes with ironic reflection that the policies equip youth poorly for the modern economy.
one_line: A satirical critique of local education policies under John Doe and Mary Smith, mocking funding cuts, faulty tech, outdated curricula and austerity.
key_facts: The satire is set after September 1, 2023, with the local government launching 'revolutionary' educational reforms to improve the local economic position.
Mr. John "Just Trust Me" Doe is the newly appointed Education Tsar, and Ms. Mary "I've Got a Plan" Smith is the chancellor.
On October 5, 2023, Mr. Doe led town hall meetings introducing a policy of slashing educational funding in areas already short of resources.
On October 27, Ms. Smith showcased new digital blackboards while the WiFi could not support more than two connections.
On November 12, 2023, the 'Omnipotent Omnitabs' tablets were announced to bridge the digital divide but proved slow with short battery life.
On November 25, 2023, fiber optics were promised for online courses; the piece mocks them as too elusive to connect to anything.
Courses are described as preparing students for jobs from the disco era, while the local labor market's needs shift unpredictably; Mr. Doe claims the ship heads toward 'prosperous new lands'.
On December 3, 2023, a 'Jargonese' language requirement was rolled out, creating confusion with buzzwords.
'Future-proof skills' are said to include critical thinking, leadership and data analysis, but the piece mocks how they are applied.
On December 15, 2023, a budget meeting celebrated educational austerity and cost cutting, leaving college freshmen baffled by overhead projectors.
Since January 2, 2024, coin-operated library doors have been introduced, with Mr. Doe and Ms. Smith certifying information beyond the gate as premium.
Murmurs from January 23, 2024 suggest Philosophy, Arts and Theatre are on the chopping block.
The article ends with a linguistics workshop that arms youth with feathered quills as a metaphor for outdated preparation for the modern economy.
